title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 3 Lesson 2: Smooth Rings Beads Pulleys custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A small smooth bead of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a smooth fixed horizontal wire. The bead is held in equilibrium by a force of magnitude $10\text{ N}$ directed upwards at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the horizontal and an opposing horizontal holding force $P$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the magnitude of the normal reaction $R_N$ exerted by the wire on the bead.

A light inextensible string passes over a fixed smooth pulley. A load of mass $3\text{ kg}$ is attached to one end and hangs vertically. The other end is pulled by a force $P$ directed at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the downward vertical, maintaining the system in equilibrium. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, state the magnitude of $P$ and explain why.

A small smooth ring of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ is threaded onto a light inextensible string whose ends are tied to two fixed points at the same level on a ceiling. In equilibrium, each string segment makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the tension $T$ in the string.

A small smooth bead of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a smooth fixed vertical wire. A force of magnitude $13\text{ N}$ acts on the bead inclined at an angle $\alpha$ above the horizontal, holding the bead in equilibrium against gravity. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the magnitude of the horizontal normal reaction $R_N$ exerted by the wire on the bead.

A light string passes over a smooth light pulley fixed at the edge of a horizontal table. One part of the string is horizontal, and the other part hangs vertically supporting a mass of $5\text{ kg}$ in equilibrium. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the magnitude of the resultant force $R$ exerted by the string on the pulley.

One end of a light string is fixed to a point $A$. The string passes through a small smooth ring of weight $16\text{ N}$, and the other end is pulled by a horizontal force $F$. In equilibrium, the segment $AR$ makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the vertical, and the other segment extends horizontally. Calculate the tension $T$ in the string.

questions.prompt: A small smooth bead $B$ of mass $m = 0.8\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a smooth fixed horizontal wire. A light inextensible string attached to the bead is inclined at $30^\circ$ above the horizontal and pulled with tension $T$. A horizontal force of magnitude $12\text{ N}$ acts on the bead in the direction opposite to the horizontal component of the string tension, keeping the bead in equilibrium. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces horizontally in equilibrium, calculate the exact tension $T$ in the string in surd form, and evaluate it correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces vertically in equilibrium, determine the magnitude of the normal reaction $R_N$ exerted by the wire on the bead, and state whether this reaction acts vertically upwards or downwards.

questions.prompt: A light inextensible string passes over a smooth pulley of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ which is supported from a horizontal ceiling by a vertical chain. A mass of $3.5\text{ kg}$ is attached to each end of the string, and both masses hang vertically in equilibrium. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the tension $T$ in the string passing over the pulley.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By considering the vertical forces acting on the pulley, calculate the tension $T_C$ in the supporting chain.

questions.prompt: A small smooth bead $B$ of mass $m = 0.5\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a smooth fixed horizontal wire. A light inextensible string attached to the bead passes over a small smooth fixed pulley located $0.8\text{ m}$ vertically above the wire. The other end of the string supports a hanging mass of $1.5\text{ kg}$ in equilibrium. The bead is held at a horizontal distance of $0.6\text{ m}$ from the point directly below the pulley by a horizontal force $F$ directed away from the pulley. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Determine the tension $T$ in the string and calculate the magnitude of the horizontal force $F$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the normal reaction $R_N$ exerted by the wire on the bead, and state whether it acts vertically upwards or downwards.

questions.prompt: A block $P$ of mass $m = 2.5\text{ kg}$ is held in equilibrium on a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. A light inextensible string attached to $P$ passes over a small smooth pulley fixed at the top of the incline, and supports a vertically hanging mass $M\text{ kg}$. The section of string between $P$ and the pulley is parallel to the line of greatest slope of the plane. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the plane on block $P$, and find the mass $M$ of the hanging load required for equilibrium.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force $F_R$ exerted by the string on the pulley, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A small smooth bead $B$ of mass $m = 0.4\text{ kg}$ is threaded onto a smooth fixed circular wire of radius $r$ held in a vertical plane with centre $C$. The highest point of the circular wire is $A$. The bead is held in equilibrium at a point $B$ by a light string attached to $A$. The radius $CB$ makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the downward vertical. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 4\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using the isosceles geometry of $\triangle CAB$, show that string $AB$ makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the vertical, and determine the angle that string $AB$ makes with the radius $CB$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving along the tangent to the circle at $B$, calculate the exact tension $T$ in the string in surd form, and evaluate it correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: By resolving radially along $CB$, determine the magnitude of the normal reaction $R_N$ exerted by the wire on the bead, and state whether it acts radially outwards from $C$ or radially inwards towards $C$.

questions.prompt: A light inextensible string has one end fixed to a horizontal ceiling at point $A$. The string passes under a light smooth movable pulley $P$ of mass $M = 2.4\text{ kg}$ which carries a suspended load, then passes over a smooth fixed pulley $B$ mounted on the ceiling, and has its free end attached to a hanging counterweight of mass $m$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (total weight of the movable pulley assembly $W = 24\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: When the two string segments supporting the movable pulley hang vertically and parallel, explain why the tension $T$ is uniform throughout the string, and calculate the tension $T$ and the counterweight mass $m$ required for equilibrium.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The ceiling supports are now spread apart so that each of the two string segments supporting the movable pulley makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with the vertical. Calculate the new tension $T'$ in the string, the new counterweight mass $m'$ required for equilibrium, and the magnitude of the resultant force $R_B$ exerted by the string on the fixed pulley $B$ if the counterweight continues to hang vertically.

questions.prompt: A light inextensible string of total length $2.0\text{ m}$ has its ends attached to two fixed points $A$ and $B$ at the same horizontal level on a ceiling, where $AB = 1.2\text{ m}$. A small smooth ring $R$ of mass $m = 1.2\text{ kg}$ is threaded on the string. A horizontal force $P$ pulls the ring to the right such that segment $AR$ makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the vertical and segment $BR$ makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the vertical. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 12\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain why the tension $T$ is uniform throughout the string, and by resolving vertically, calculate the exact tension $T$ in surd form and evaluate it correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving horizontally, calculate the magnitude of the horizontal pulling force $P$ in exact surd form and correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: The horizontal pulling force is now removed ($P = 0$), allowing the ring to settle into its natural symmetrical equilibrium position. Calculate the vertical depth $h$ of the ring below the ceiling and determine the new tension $T_0$ in the string.
